chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Uthman and Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to proclaim Takbeer five times over a group of people, and over another group four times. So when he proclaimed Takbeer four times over a man, they would accuse him, meaning of hypocrisy.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet vary the number of Takbeers in funeral prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (SAW) variable practice in funeral prayers, where offering four Takbeers served as a specific indicator of the deceased's suspected hypocrisy (nifaq), distinguishing them from the standard five. This variation underscores the theological significance of the prayer as a witness to the individual's spiritual state, a concept deeply rooted in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the intercessory nature of the funeral rite.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad Bin Usman and Hisham Bin Salim, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww used to exclaim five Takbeers upon a group of people, and upon another group of people, four (Takbeers). So when hesaww exclaimed four (Takbeers) upon a man, they (people) would accuse him (the deceased) of hypocrisy’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman and Hisham ibn Salim who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah would say five Takbir for certain people, and four Takbir for other groups of people. When he (the Messenger of Allah) would say four Takbir in the Salah (prayer) for a dead man, he (the deceased) was suspected of hypocrisy.”
